question.text: A silver sphere of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and work function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>4.7</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math> is suspended from an insulating thread in free-space. It is under continuous illumination of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> wavelength electromagnetic waves. As photoelectrons are emitted, the sphere gets charged and acquires a potential. The maximum number of photoelectrons emitted from the sphere is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi></msup></math> (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo><</mo><mn>10</mn></math>). The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Photo emission will stop when potential on silver sphere becomes equal to the stopping potential.

Stopping potential

= hc λ - w

=6.2-4.7=1.5 eV

V = Kq r = 1 . 5 = K × n × e r

⇒    n = 1 . 5 × 1 0 - 2 1 . 6 × 1 0 - 1 9 × 9 × 1 0 9 = 1 . 0 5 × 1 0 7

⇒     z=7

Therefore answer is 7.
